I had initially planned on skipping this one; huge fallout fan (and Elder Scrolls for that matter) but FO76 just did not look like something I'd enjoy. After a few positive beta-reviews and watching some streams I caved though. I dunno, too much of a fanboy or just poor impulse control. Had the chance to try it out last night and was pretty... "whelmed"? Neither under- nor over, just whelmed.

I initially thought the multiplayer/PvP thing would be the biggest issue, but it's really not. First thing I did was disable voice chat; that significantly increased my enjoyment. Got attacked a few times but the unilateral PvP damage reduction is ridiculous, so I could just pop into the social menu and "Ignore" the player without taking any noticeable damage at all. The only MP annoyance left I guess would be the lack of "immersion" from having a bunch of retards with names like "DildoKing666" jumping around in their underwear tea-bagging radroaches but I guess I could ascribe that to brain damage from the radiation.

The lack of NPCs was more jarring; maybe it's because I've played FO3/FONV/FO4 so much and have come to expect bumping into NPCs everywhere but the world feels so empty. It kinda reminded me of a bug that sometimes popped up in WoW when the servers were having issues and the world rendered in after zoning but the NPCs didn't. Walking around a place that felt familiar but was completely abandoned just felt wrong and unsettling.

Then there is the holotapes. My god, the holotapes. They are everywhere and they ramble on forever! And you kinda have to listen to them if you want to make sense of the story/quests. Not a fan of this method of storytelling... But I guess you have to do it like this when you don't have NPCs.. The story itself (what I've seen of it so far anyway) isn't half bad though.

Another thing that worries me is how buggy the game is this close to release. I really hope we are playing on a very old build of the game engine, because I seriously doubt they'll be able to fix all these bugs in two weeks. The game itself is unstable, had a few CTDs and one or two freezes. It's horribly optimized in places. some zones like the airport lagged really badly despite me being alone there. Quest markers randomly stop updating, mobs get stuck in terrain and objects, the AI is retarded.. It's going to be a complete mess well past release if this is a current build of the game.

I'll be playing again this weekend to try to get more into the game; maybe try to find some friends who play and see if "embracing" the multiplayer makes it better. But I really don't know how long I'll stick with this one, might mothball it until private servers and mods get added in a year or so.
